title: Disable or Modify Tools: Disable or Modify Cloud Log
shortTitle: Disable or Modify Tools: Disable or Modify Cloud Log
summary: Cloud Log tampering degrades the audit record in a cloud tenant or subscription, where visibility is a product feature rather than a fixed property of the host. Adversaries with sufficient permissions reconfigure the collection plane itself: disabling or trimming a multi-region trail, removing the notification topics that deliver findings, turning off log file validation or encryption settings, or excluding services and regions from capture. In productivity suites the equivalent is per-user audit bypass and licence downgrade, both of which stop generating mailbox audit records without touching a security tool. The result is a silent hole rather than a deleted file, so detection rests on configuration auditing and on continuity checks: comparing the current logging configuration against baseline, alerting on changes to trail, topic, and audit settings, and watching for unexpected gaps or unmonitored regions in delivered logs. Identity records showing who changed the configuration are the primary corroborating artefact.

beginner.definition: Cloud services keep records of what users do, and those records can be switched off. This technique means an attacker changes the logging settings in a cloud account so their actions are not recorded. They may disable a log, stop its delivery, or exclude a whole region. No tool is broken in an obvious way.
beginner.whyItMatters: In the cloud you often have no machine to inspect, only the provider's records. If logging is reduced, the attacker can create accounts, read data, or move files without leaving a trail. This is easy to miss, because the account still looks healthy. Guarding the logging settings is therefore as important as guarding the data itself.
howItWorks: The attacker obtains cloud credentials with permission to manage logging.
They check which audit trails and log deliveries are currently active.
They disable a trail, or stop it covering every region and service.
They may remove the alert topics, or turn off validation and encryption of log files.
In a mail service, they can bypass auditing for chosen users or lower their licence level.
They carry out their real activity while the record is incomplete or absent.
beginner.example: Think of a bus company where each depot sends a daily sheet of trips to head office. Someone with the right password simply stops one depot from sending its sheet, and cancels the reminder emails. The buses keep running and the drivers behave normally. Head office only notices because one route's paperwork never arrives.
takeaways: Treat logging configuration as a high-value asset and alert when it changes.
Check that trails cover every region and that alert delivery still works.
Unexplained gaps or missing periods in delivered logs deserve investigation.

objectives: Explain how cloud log tampering differs from the parent technique Disable or Modify Tools.
Describe common changes such as disabling a trail, region, or alert delivery.
Explain how per-user audit bypass and licence changes suppress records in productivity suites.
Identify the identity and configuration artefacts that record who changed logging.
Describe continuity checks that reveal silent gaps in collected cloud logs.
